gap.description: On the head keyword 'education visa thailand' itself, none of the top 5 ranking pages (law firm, embassy, 2 language schools, travel-agency blog) mention the DTV visa or frame the decision as a choice between two distinct visa vehicles — they only explain the ED visa in isolation, usually for language-school students, with at most a passing one-line nod to Muay Thai as an eligible ED category (aaathai.school). A real ED-vs-DTV comparison specifically for Muay Thai practitioners does exist, but on separate long-tail URLs outside this SERP (muaythaivisathailand.com/dtv-vs-ed-vs-tourist by Kru Chart/Sor.Dechapant school, muaythaifever.com, ask.in.th) — these are gym-affiliated, reasonably strong on E-E-A-T (named author, MOE/SAT license number, real gym-admin pain points, tables, 34-item FAQ), but promotional (repeated WhatsApp CTAs funneling to their own visa-prep service), missing named case examples of a real student choosing one path, and light on itemized long-run cost comparison. Wildcat's opening: rank on the informational head term with a comparison the current top 5 skip entirely, written by an operator (Meaw) who files real DTV dossiers without promising outcomes, and link out to the existing 12-URL DTV silo instead of re-doing the cost breakdown.

weakness: Every top-5 result for 'education visa thailand' is either a generic institutional page or a language-school funnel — none written for someone specifically choosing between ED and DTV as a Muay Thai practitioner

The strongest direct ED-vs-DTV-for-Muay-Thai competitors (MTVT/Kru Chart, muaythaifever) are promotional gym-visa-service pages with commercial CTAs, not neutral comparison content, and lack real named applicant case studies
No result on this SERP explains the DTV 'soft power qualifying activity' status of Muay Thai specifically, or how that changes the calculus vs. the ED visa's school-attendance model

None of the top 5 cite Thai MFA/immigration sourcing directly for the DTV eligibility criteria (accredited-gym requirement, 500,000 THB financial proof, 2025 exclusion of language schools from soft-power categories)
recommended_angle: Write the article as a decision framework, not a cost breakdown: 'ED visa vs DTV for Muay Thai training in Thailand — which one fits your situation.' Center it on the two visa vehicles' structural trade-offs (ED = single accredited school, mandatory attendance, ~80-100k THB/year, 90-day renewal cycle vs DTV = 5-year multi-entry, 180+180 day stays, no attendance requirement, allows remote work, Muay Thai as a recognized soft-power activity), sourced against current MFA/immigration criteria. Carry E-E-A-T through Meaw's real experience preparing DTV dossiers for Wildcat guests — process and documentation reality, zero promise of visa approval — without repeating the numeric cost breakdown already owned by dtv-visa-cost-breakdown and dtv-vs-tourist-visa-runs-cost; link out to those and to /dtv-visa/long-stay-training for the depth. Differentiate from the existing gym-affiliated comparisons by staying non-promotional (no visa-service upsell) and by using this as top-of-funnel content that feeds the DTV silo rather than duplicating it.
